prompt:
A designed desktop website first viewport, landscape 16:9, approximately 1440 by 810 pixels. This is a real BitVault landing-page UI screenshot, not a poster, not a billboard, not an art print, not a magazine cover.

Page structure, named in reading order:

(1) Top bar, full width, about 64 pixels tall: a kraft paper / manila-envelope textured navigation strip. Left: wordmark BitVault in dark warm ink #1A1714, quiet industrial lettering. Right: a single solid rectangular CTA button labeled Get the APK, forest green #2F5D50 fill, cream #E7D7B8 lettering. No extra nav links, no hamburger, no search.

(2) Hero object owns the first screen: occupying the left-center, roughly 55 percent of the viewport, a full-scale photographed USB-C flash stick treated as a labeled .vault file. Brushed USB-C metal body, heat-shrink wrap label, manila kraft tag, ballpoint handwriting that reads PHONE-A → PHONE-B and .vault. Product still-life photography, giant, tactile, sitting on a dark warm charcoal #1A1714 workshop surface. This object is larger than everything else.

(3) Type to the right of the stick, mid-height, readable website copy not poster type: headline You copy one file. That is the sync. Supporting line in smaller type: BitVault is one encrypted file you carry, not a product you log into. No account. No server. No cloud. No INTERNET permission. Palette of cream #E7D7B8 type and brass #C4A574 accents on #1A1714.

(4) Lower right, clearly smaller than the USB stick: a modest Android phone as destination, not hero chrome. The phone shows a simple file-received or lock state, never a SaaS dashboard, never analytics, never a settings grid. The stick is going to the phone.

Materials: brushed USB-C metal, heat-shrink labels, manila envelope, ballpoint on kraft. Lighting: close workshop still-life, directional, no neon, no volumetric fog.

Do not include: crypto-hype, blockchain cubes, cloud orbs, padlock icons in gold, fake testimonials, star ratings, Play Store badges, invented rankings, login forms, account CTAs, prices, dates, or any product name other than BitVault.
